working_title: England's Forgotten Golf County: A Practical Guide to Playing Lincolnshire
angle: Lincolnshire punches well above its weight as a golf destination, pairing one of England's finest heathland courses (Woodhall Spa's Hotchkin) with a genuinely underrated links (Seacroft at Skegness) and a stay-and-play coastal option (North Shore). The post makes the practical case for a two- or three-night Lincolnshire golf trip, explaining how to stitch the courses together logically and what visitors actually need to know before booking.
research_notes:
- Lincolnshire described as 'England's great golfing undercard' with distinct course clusters around Woodhall Spa inland and the northern/eastern coast (Skegness area).
- Woodhall Spa (National Golf Centre, home of England Golf): two courses — the Hotchkin and the Bracken. Hotchkin is the headline act, recently renovated by Tom Doak to restore heathland character. Ranked 12th in Golf Monthly's UK & Ireland Top 100. Handicap limit of 24 men / 36 ladies applies for the Hotchkin. England Golf-affiliated members receive a discounted green fee (bring CDH number or handicap cert). Advance booking and a non-refundable £20-per-golfer deposit required. Located approx 20 miles from Lincoln. Online and phone booking available.
- Seacroft Golf Club, Skegness: traditional links founded 1895, described as a 'hidden gem' on the Lincolnshire coast. Adjacent to Gibraltar Point Nature Reserve, itself a Natural England Site of Special Scientific Interest. Out-and-back layout, 6,492 yards, par 71. Fast-draining soil means virtually year-round play on normal tees and greens. 75 bunkers, narrow hogsback fairways, coastal wind a major factor. Rated by National Club Golfer as 6th best value club in GB & Ireland (out of 250). Green fees as last reported (2023 data, confirm with club): approx £60 weekday, £70 weekend in high season — treat these as indicative, not guaranteed current figures; readers should check directly with the club. Handicap cert required, advance booking advised.
- North Shore Hotel & Golf Club, Skegness: James Braid-designed 18-hole course (1910), par 71, 6,216 yards, mixture of links and parkland holes. Stay-and-play hotel on site (34 en-suite rooms), Braid Bar and James Restaurant. Positioned on the coast, views across the Wash to Norfolk. Open to visitors. Casual fees described as starting from £28 by a third-party source — do not use this as a confirmed current figure; direct with club recommended.
- Lincolnshire is a notably dry county by English standards ('the drier side of Britain').
- Good access via East Midlands Airport and road from both North and South; city of Lincoln nearby for non-golfers.
- Woodhall Spa village is a quiet, characterful base with a heritage dating to Victorian mineral water spa discovery.
- A logical trip structure: arrive Lincoln/Woodhall Spa area, play Hotchkin (and/or Bracken), move to coast, play Seacroft and/or North Shore.
must_avoid:
- Do not quote specific current green fees as confirmed facts for Seacroft or North Shore — figures found are from third-party or dated 2023 sources; describe as indicative and direct readers to contact clubs directly. Woodhall Spa green fee structure is confirmed on the club's own site but specific per-round prices were not visible in search results, so do not invent a figure.
- Do not fabricate any quotes from players, pros, or reviewers.
- No betting, health/injury, or financial-advice content.
- No affiliate links unless Woodhall Spa, Seacroft, or North Shore are in the approved-partners list; mention all three informationally if not pre-approved.
- No invented personal anecdotes about playing these courses.
- No em dashes anywhere in the post.
- UK English spelling throughout (favour, colour, recognise, etc.).
